text.p: Aerospace optic and laser systems maker Avimo Group Ltd said on Thursday the outlook for 1997 was encouraging.

"With order books at record levels, the Apache contract beginning to come on stream at Avimo Taunton and the expected contribution from Amarel, the outlook for the coming year is encouraging," Avimo said in a statement accompanying its full year results.
The group's outstanding order book as at the year ended September 30, 1996 was up 92 percent from the previous year to Singapore $226.9 million.
Avimo said this included the award of a S$100 million contract on the Apache helicopter programme at Avimo Taunton in the United Kingdom and a S$34 million order for night vision optics from the U.S.
On November 15, Avimo completed its acquisition of 80 percent of Amarel Precision Instruments Inc, a U.S. specialist optics company.
On Thursday, Avimo reported that full year net profit rose 28.83 percent to about S$8 million on a turnover of S$117.88 million.
Avimo said the improvement in the group's performance was mainly due to a significant increase in sales volume and operational efficency at Avimo Electro-Optics.
Progress at Avimo Taunton after an upgrade programme for the British Army's reconnaissance vehicles in Bosnia also boosted performance, it said.
Avimo said the progress was dampened by continuing difficulties at Avimo Malaysia which faced low operating efficiency due to high labour turnover.

It said performance was also dampened by the inability of Singapore's metal finishing business to recover some of the customers lost as a result of a fire in March in the anodising line and a slowdown in the electronics industry.

The company said it had made an extraordinary provision of S$1.48 million to cover the expected costs of closure of its Penang facility in Malaysia. But this was offset by a surplus extraordinary provision relating to the closure of the aerospace machining operations which are no longer required following its withdrawal from Malaysia.
Avimo is 38 percent owned by British defence manufacturer Alvis Plc.
